tagline: Alpha Notion-driven scheduler for posting threads to X, with Bluesky claimed but unconfirmed.
description: Threaduler is a small Python project that publishes social posts from a Notion database. You write posts and their metadata in Notion, using a template database the author shares, and the tool reads that content and sends it to the networks. The README describes it as a 0.1 alpha that works but may have hiccups, and says it works with X and Bluesky and that LinkedIn is coming, but its own roadmap still lists Bluesky integration as unchecked, so treat Bluesky as unconfirmed. The template includes examples of threads and quote posts. To run it, you install Poetry, create a Notion integration, get Notion and X API keys, clone the repository, install dependencies and put the keys in a .env file. There is no Docker image or web interface in the README, so you run it yourself and keep it scheduled yourself. The licence is MIT. It could replace a paid scheduler like Hootsuite only for a solo writer who lives in Notion and mainly posts to X. It has none of the team features of Hootsuite, such as approvals, analytics or inbox. Development looks inactive and the community is tiny, so treat it as a starting point, not a supported product.
strengths: Uses Notion as the editor and content store, so drafts stay in a tool you may already use
Handles threads and quote posts, with example posts in the template database
MIT licence and a small Python codebase you can read and change
Aims at X from a single source of posts, with Bluesky support claimed but unconfirmed
limits: Labelled 0.1 alpha by its author, with unspecified rough edges expected
X is the confirmed network; Bluesky is claimed but still on the roadmap, and LinkedIn is marked as coming
Needs your own Notion and X API keys, and an installed Poetry environment
The README gives no Docker setup, web interface, approvals, analytics or team features
Tiny community and signs of inactive development
bestFor: A solo writer who already plans posts in Notion, is comfortable with Python, and posts mainly to X.
